method: 20 read-only domain auditors, each required to cite file:line and to trace a caller chain from a real runtime entry point (registered Temporal workflow/activity, mounted FastAPI route, console-script CLI verb, installer/systemd unit). Every production-reachable claim was then re-checked by an independent adversarial verifier defaulting to REFUTED; a refuted claim is recorded here as test-only, with claimed_status and break_point kept.

status_vocabulary.production-reachable: a real caller chain exists from a runtime entry point
status_vocabulary.test-only: correct code whose only callers are tests — a FAILING condition for pre-live readiness
status_vocabulary.sealed: a deliberate fail-closed default is in place and nothing overrides it in production
status_vocabulary.simulated: only the Simulator plugin implements it
status_vocabulary.fake-only: only a bounded fake implements it
status_vocabulary.declared-unimplemented: a name, protocol, enum member or docstring with no implementation

areas.area: Privileged worker installation and packaging (apps/management/secp_management, apps/deployment, apps/commissioning, packaging/installer scripts) — branch feature/secp-https-discovery-integration at C…
areas.summary: SECP has a genuine, production-wired installer *sequencer* — `secpctl worker install --write --confirm` really renders a hardened systemd unit, writes it through the hardened openat filesystem, drives systemctl through the pinned-executable seam, persists a durable identity with read-back, verifies restart, and removes the unit on failure. What it does NOT have is anything to install: the unit's `ExecStart=/opt/secp/worker/bin/secp-worker` is produced by no code, no console script, no archive extractor, no .deb/.rpm/install.sh, and `secp_worker.main` does not even accept the `--role/--task-queue` argv the unit passes; the dedicated `secp-worker` account is only *required*, never created; and the fixed production inputs the composition reads from `/var/lib/secp/bootstrap/` are seeded only by a test module. So the installer does not deterministically construct the runtime tree — it validates a tree an administrator must have built by hand, and refuses (`installer_worker_runtime_absent`, `production_input_unavailable`) otherwise. No CI job exercises the worker-installer adapters against real systemd: the one real-systemd root job covers only the *bootstrap* adapter's disabled-operator unit, and the acceptance workflow states in its own header that the worker-install stage "has NO producing code yet".

capabilities.name: Orphan state cleanup (worker host)
capabilities.evidence: The only orphan sweep in the tree is controller-side: engine.py:2651 _finalization_cleanup_absent independently probes the finalization recovery journal and every staging/backup handle and gates the commit at engine.py:2705 (`recovery_required` when residue remains). For the WORKER host there is nothing equivalent. The installer's replay guard, worker_installer.py:511-532 _verify_not_replayed, REFUSES (`installer_enrollment_replayed`) when a stale durable record is found — it never cleans it. Nothing sweeps an orphaned /etc/systemd/system/secp-worker-*.service, /opt/secp/worker/state, /var/lib/secp/worker-enrollment/state marker, or a stale worker-installation-identity.json; the rollback plan (engine.py:3576-3598) touches only the five bootstrap documents.
capabilities.gap: A worker host left half-installed (unit written, enrollment failed, rollback's own removal failed — which worker_installer.py:578-588 deliberately SWALLOWS so the original error survives) has no cleanup path. The next install attempt refuses on the stale record rather than reconciling it.

areas.area: Durable worker enrollment, registration and verification anchors (worktree C:/security-environment-control-plane-worktrees/integration, branch feature/secp-https-discovery-integration, HEAD 78e1da7)
areas.summary: The durable worker-enrollment substrate is genuinely production-reachable: four tables + a signed-offer table, a strict re-validating repository, a mounted FastAPI router, a registered Temporal sweep activity, and a secpctl-driven worker-side store all connect end to end, and the controller identity that supplies the trust anchor and expected release digest is written by a real `secpctl controller install` chain. The discovery-snapshot verification layer is the opposite: `ExpectedWorkerRegistration`, `verify_discovery_snapshot`, `VerifiedDiscoverySnapshot`, the worker's `run_full_discovery` snapshot producer, the second `verify_discovery_binding` verifier family, and `build_pending_sdn_document` have zero non-test callers, and the discovery engine that *does* run in production emits an evidence dict with no signature, binding or signer at all — so there is no production loader that reads a durable registration in order to verify a signed discovery snapshot, because in production no signed discovery snapshot is ever produced. The evidence-driven enrollment exchange that would exercise the release-digest and signed-offer paths is sealed by the shipped `SealedEnrollmentOfferSignerClient` default.

areas.area: Credential reference lifecycle (ResolutionPurpose, WorkerSecretResolver, SealedDiscoveryCredentialResolver, credential-reference storage)
areas.summary: The durable side of the lifecycle is real and reachable: `ExecutionTarget.secret_ref` plus two dedicated operation references are org+target-scoped columns, each shadowed by an opaque versioned `CredentialBinding`, and rotation is reachable from two mounted FastAPI routes and is forced by an ORM `before_flush` hook plus a PostgreSQL trigger, with audit on create and rotate. Revocation of a binding is a declared-but-unwritten enum member, deletion is sealed, and there is no revoke/delete audit action. The strict resolution seam is not reachable: the shipped preflight chain is sealed by a denying identity verifier before `resolve()`, the OpenBao adapter and the whole HTTPS-discovery credential path (`SealedDiscoveryCredentialResolver`, `build_discovery_resolution_request`, `run_full_discovery`) have no non-test caller at all — while a second, older path, `EnvSecretResolver` inside the registered `discover_activity`, does resolve a real credential from `os.environ` and hand it to a real Proxmox HTTPS transport with none of the purpose/contract/lease/activation/audit machinery applied.

areas.area: OpenTofu execution path (apps/worker/secp_worker/{plan_gen,provisioning,deployment}, infra/)
areas.summary: No shipped code path in this repository ever executes the OpenTofu binary. Exactly one OpenTofu-adjacent runtime entry point is production-reachable — the registered `real_plan_generation_activity` — and it refuses at the plan-execution composition gate before any filesystem access, render, secret resolution, executor construction, or subprocess; the shipped `SealedPlanExecutionCompositionProvider` can never return an enabled composition, and the only alternative (the operator bootstrap) dead-ends in `run_operator_worker`, which is hard-sealed AND contains no Temporal `Worker` construction even if unsealed. The whole apply/destroy family (`OpenTofuRunner`, `run_real_provisioning`, the Proxmox apply/destroy/reset/residue/reconcile gates) has zero production callers — it is imported only by `*/tests/*` — and is additionally sealed by `_B1A_SUBPROCESS_SEALED = True`. The safety engineering is genuinely strong and unusually well-evidenced (argv-only grammar, executable-object pinning via `/proc/self/fd`, closed child env, bounded streaming I/O, process-group kill, exact-hash approval binding), but as of this branch it is machinery whose only executor is the test suite; there are no `.tf` files, no `.terraform.lock.hcl`, and no OpenTofu module bundle anywhere in the repo or under `infra/`.

areas.area: Topology compilation and per-team network design
areas.summary: There are three distinct "scenario + team count -> topology" compilers, and none of them delivers the full per-team network design in production. The Simulator compiler is the only one whose output is ever realised, and it only writes database rows (per-team /24 + host IPs, no VLAN, no firewall, no segment roles). The manifest compiler (`_build_topology`) is genuinely route-reachable and produces per-team CIDR/VMID/placement, but has no VLAN, no segment roles and no isolation rules. The full design — per-team SDN VNets, unique VLAN tags, attacker/vulnerable/scoring segments, ordered deny rules and a first-match reachability proof — exists only in the Proxmox compiler, which IS reachable from mounted routes but can never return a plan in production: its sole required input (a `TargetObservation` recorded as a `proxmox_observation_recorded` lifecycle event) has no producer anywhere outside tests, its `attach_to_manifest` seam into the worker renderer is called only by tests, and the worker's range provider registry does not know the name `proxmox` at all. Storage/corporate-network prohibitions are absent from every compiler.

areas.area: The five-stage SDN activation path (prepared → pending_observed → activation_authorized → activated → verified), plus destroy semantics

areas.area: Guest (VM/LXC) deployment — Proxmox plugin and worker provisioning/deployment trees
areas.summary: No production caller chain in this worktree can create a Proxmox guest. The Proxmox plugin is read-only by construction (plan/apply/reset/destroy raise `UnsupportedCapabilityError` at plugins/proxmox/secp_plugin_proxmox/plugin.py:149-159), there is no Proxmox `RangeProvider` in the worker registry (apps/worker/secp_worker/range/__init__.py:36-37 raises `KeyError` for any name but `local_docker`), no OpenTofu `apply` verb exists anywhere on a production path (the plan-only command grammar admits only init/plan/show/validate/providers, apps/worker/secp_worker/plan_gen/process_boundary.py:113; `_B1A_SUBPROCESS_SEALED = True` at provisioning/process_executor.py:123), and the rich desired-state compiler can never emit a topology because nothing outside tests writes the observation event it requires (`EVENT_OBSERVATION` at services/proxmox_lifecycle.py:121 has test-only writers, so compile_plan always returns BlockedPlan via :604-605). Three distinct Proxmox renderers exist and must not be conflated: the full range bundle (guests, disks, NICs, cloud-init, SDN, firewall) is test-only; the inert `labfake_*` fixture targets a deliberately fake provider; and the only renderer on a production-wired activity emits exactly one LXC container and sits behind a sealed composition gate. Guest hardware beyond CPU/memory/disk/NIC — BIOS/UEFI, TPM, boot order, startup order, snapshots, passthroug…

areas.area: Guest configuration plane (configuring the inside of a deployed range guest)
areas.summary: SECP has NO production-reachable mechanism that can install a package, write a file, run a command, or create a user inside a deployed range guest. The single most complete artifact is a cloud-init renderer in `apps/worker/secp_worker/provisioning/adapters/proxmox_bundle.py:427-463`, and it emits only a static IP, optional DNS, a login username and SSH public keys — it has no `user_data`, `runcmd`, `write_files` or `packages` field anywhere in the tree, and its only callers are `apps/api/tests/*`. Everything downstream of it is sealed (`tofu apply` refused, `_B1A_SUBPROCESS_SEALED = True`), the production plan-generation renderer structurally forbids provisioners and emits one LXC with `started = false`, `BootstrapOperation` carries only key/description/timeout with no command field and is always empty in production, and Ansible/WinRM/Sysprep/guest-agent/image-baking are entirely absent. A workload in the scenario schema is `{name, kind, image, network, count, vulnerabilityPacks}` with `additionalProperties: false` — there is no field that could drive guest configuration.

capabilities.name: cloud-init user-data that installs a package, writes a file, or runs a command inside a guest
capabilities.evidence: The only cloud-init generator in the tree is `_render_cloud_init` at apps/worker/secp_worker/provisioning/adapters/proxmox_bundle.py:427-463. It emits exactly three things into the bpg provider's `initialization {}` block: `dns` (proxmox_bundle.py:443-448), `ip_config.ipv4.address`/`gateway` (proxmox_bundle.py:450-456), and `user_account { username, keys }` (proxmox_bundle.py:458-461). A repo-wide search for `user_data`/`userdata` returns NO files at all; searches for `runcmd`, `write_files`, `packages:`, `cidata`, `config_drive`, `nocloud`, `meta-data`, `seed.iso` return nothing in apps/, plugins/ or contracts/. `CloudInitSpec` (apps/api/secp_api/range_providers/proxmox_model.py:530-553) has exactly five fields — user, ssh_authorized_keys, nameservers, search_domain, gateway — and no field for a script, file or package.
capabilities.gap: There is no code path anywhere in the repository that can place arbitrary content, a package list, or a command into a guest's first boot. Cloud-init here is a network+login configurator only.

The break is on the producing/executing side: there is NO production writer for the Proxmox observation-of-record event, NO Proxmox range provider (`get_provider` raises KeyError for "proxmox"), the whole Proxmox apply/verify/reset/residue gate family and the entire five-stage SDN activation model are imported only by tests, and the operator worker that would run real OpenTofu is hard-sealed by a code constant with no Worker-construction code behind it. So the operator can drive the journey up to authorization; past that point every read is structurally pinned at "undetermined" in a real deployment.

areas.summary: The operation-lifecycle half of this area is genuinely production-reachable and unusually honest: range operation identity, durable status, per-step progress, lease-derived staleness, failure code/message and an authorized abandon path all have real HTTP routes and a real Temporal activity behind them, and staleness is derived on read from durable columns rather than written by a sweeper. The observation half is much weaker than it reads: the worker-liveness projection has a production WRITE path but no reader anywhere outside tests, so no operator or client can ever see a last-observed time; and every Proxmox worker-recorded stage (observation, verification, reset dispositions, residue, reconciliation) has a mounted read route that will report `undetermined`/`absent` forever because nothing in production writes those events and there is no Proxmox range provider at all. A controller restart cannot manufacture freshness — the observation registry is process-local and restarts to `unobserved`, and no timestamp anywhere is derived from process start — but two liveness-shaped claims are made with zero observation behind them: the plugin `healthy` badge is a hardcoded `True`, and the staging-deployment `verify` operation kind returns success unconditionally.

areas.summary: The Alembic chain is a single linear 36-revision chain with head `a1d4f7c2e9b6` (computed from the 36 files' revision/down_revision pairs; the only base is `09a75fd21cf8` and no file names `a1d4f7c2e9b6` as its down_revision). Those 36 revisions create 79 tables, and the ORM declares 92 — the exact 13-table difference is the entire range/competition family in `apps/api/secp_api/range_models.py`, which has NO migration, is NOT imported by `secp_api/models.py` (so Alembic autogenerate cannot even see it), and is created only by the dev/test-only `Base.metadata.create_all` at `main.py:148`. That family is the durable spine of the Proxmox range lifecycle — instances, provider resources, operations, the lifecycle event log that stores the apply/reset/destroy plan-hash approvals, and the residue/teardown evidence — and it is fully wired to mounted routes and a registered Temporal workflow, so a production database migrated to head cannot serve it. Of the directive's five required concepts: plan-hash approval exists (three migrated tables) but NOT for the Proxmox path; credential reference is deliberately unrepresentable by design; discovery-operation authorization exists but carries no generation; SDN activation authorization and a migrated residue verification record are absent.

areas.area: Plugin capability contract (contracts/plugin-api) and the Proxmox plugin's real capabilities (plugins/proxmox), compared with the Simulator plugin — worktree C:/security-environment-control-plane-wor…
areas.summary: The v1 plugin contract declares ten capabilities; the Proxmox plugin implements exactly one end-to-end (discover, plus the validate_target it calls internally), hard-refuses the four mutating ones, and has two implemented-but-uncalled methods (validate, status). The Proxmox plugin has NO mutation path in production: plan/apply/reset/destroy raise UnsupportedCapabilityError before any request, its only HTTP transport is GET-only, and it is never registered in the control-plane plugin registry at all — only the built-in Simulator is, so orchestration's deploy/reset/destroy can only ever resolve to the Simulator. `plugins/proxmox/secp_plugin_proxmox/mutation_transport.py` is a complete, well-hardened POST/PUT/DELETE transport that NO production module imports — its only importers are two test modules and three boundary-guard denylists; the worker's deployment engine deliberately wires its own `_SealedMutationTransport` instead. Two contract claims in the docstrings are not true of the code: "the control plane checks capability support before dispatching" is implemented nowhere, and `reconcile`/`collect-artifacts` are enum members with no protocol method and no implementation.
